newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain union, employers labour reform plan detailed.
newsitem.headline: Spain union, employers labour reform plan detailed.

text.p: Spain's unions and employers revealed their proposals for labour reforms on Wednesday, after months of intense talks.
The changes must still be approved by the two sides' executive committees, although they are expected to gain overwhelming approval.
The following is a list of contracts -- the key area for reform -- that will replace the current framework of 18 contracts:
1. PERMANENT CONTRACT
- Four-year contract.
- Aimed at unemployed with difficulty integrating into market: young people between 18 and 29, those unemployed for more than a year, people over 45 years, the handicapped.
- Aimed at workers on temporary or fixed-period contracts.

- Dismissal terms: where employer has cited "objective causes" for dismissal, but deemed by court to be unfair -- 33 days salary per year worked (instead of current 45), prorating by months if less than one year, and up to a maxiumum of 24 months (instead of current 42).
2. TRAINING CONTRACTS
Aimed at easing insertion of youths into job market and those with lack of training.
a) TRAINING CONTRACT
- Aimed at 16 to 21 year-olds and handicapped of all ages without training needed for skills contract.
- Minimum duration: six months, maximum: two years.
b) SKILLS CONTRACT
- Remain the same as existing skills contract.
- Aimed at those with professional training, degrees and specialists.
Unions and employers propose that legislator create incentives to convert these two contracts into permanent contracts at expiry.
3. TEMPORARY CONTRACTS
a) CONTRACT FOR FIXED WORK OR SERVICES
b) CONTRACT FOR WORK WHICH IS TEMPORARY FOR PRODUCTION REASONS
- When circumstances in market are unpredictable, for example during period of high demand.
- Maximum duration: six months within a 12-month period.
However, unions and employers want to reduce use of these contracts.
The two sides are also proposing elimination of current contracts which apply to creation of new business.
4. PART-TIME WORK
a) PART-TIME CONTRACT
- Applies to work of less than 12 hours a week or 48 hours a month.
b) CONTRACT FOR FIXED-DISCONTINUOUS WORK
c) RELIEF CONTRACT
Other areas for planned reform include the following:
* Rewriting and clarification of "objective reasons" an employer can give for dismissing worker. Employer can give following reasons:
- Economic: where company faced with negative economic situation.
- Technical, organisational, production reasons: where company faced with problems in good functioning of company.
* New agreement on collective bargaining.
* Creation of commission made up of union, employer and government representatives to follow progress of accord.
